import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism
$\varphi$ of prime order $p$ such that every subgroup
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ is nilpotent?
Here an automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is splitting if
$g g^{\varphi} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for every $g \in G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.59»

/--
Let $p$ be prime and let $G$ be a $p'$-group, meaning that no element of $G$
has order $p$. Suppose that $G$ admits an automorphism $\varphi$ of order
exactly $p$ such that
$g g^{\varphi} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for every $g \in G$, and that
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ is nilpotent for
every $g \in G$. Is $G$ locally nilpotent; that is, is every finitely
generated subgroup of $G$ nilpotent?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (G : Type) [Group G] (φ : G ≃* G),
      (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p) →
      orderOf φ = p →
      (∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map (fun i ↦ φ^[i] g)).prod = 1) →
      (∀ g : G, Group.IsNilpotent
        (Subgroup.closure (Set.range (fun i : Fin p ↦ φ^[i] g)))) →
      ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.59»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted a p'-group, as required by the decomposition, as a group with no element of order p: ∀ g, orderOf g ≠ p. This allows elements of infinite order.
Expressed exact prime order of the automorphism as orderOf φ = p, separately from p.Prime.
Expressed the splitting identity as the ordered List product over List.range p, so the noncommuting factors occur as g, φ(g), ..., φ^(p-1)(g).
Expressed the orbit-generated subgroup as Subgroup.closure of the range indexed by Fin p.
Expressed local nilpotence as nilpotence of every finitely generated subgroup H, using Mathlib's Subgroup.FG and Group.IsNilpotent. The nilpotency class may vary with H.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ are nilpotent?

An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is called *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^{2}} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

Here $g^{\varphi}$ denotes the image $\varphi(g)$, a $p'$-group is a (possibly infinite)
group with no element of order $p$, and a group is locally nilpotent if all of its
finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.59»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNilpotent_of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi$ has order exactly $p$ and
$g \cdot g^{\varphi} \cdot g^{\varphi^{2}} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$,
where $g^{\varphi} = \varphi(g)$. -/
def IsSplittingAutomorphism (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  orderOf φ = p ∧ ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

/-- The subgroup $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ of $G$
generated by the first $p$ images of $g$ under the powers of $\varphi$. -/
def orbitSubgroup (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) (g : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin p => (φ ^ (i : ℕ)) g)

/--
Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ are nilpotent?

Here a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$ (the group $G$ need not be
periodic), and the nilpotency class of
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ may depend on $g$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime →
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p) →
        ∀ φ : MulAut G, IsSplittingAutomorphism p φ →
          (∀ g : G, Group.IsNilpotent (orbitSubgroup p φ g)) →
          IsLocallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.59»

# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ are nilpotent?

An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is called *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^{2}} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

to be periodic: a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$. A group is locally

namespace Kourovka.«10.59»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ of a group $G$ is *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^{2}} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$, where
$g^{\varphi}$ is the image of $g$ under $\varphi$. The product is taken in the group $G$,
in the order $g, \varphi(g), \varphi^2(g), \ldots, \varphi^{p-1}(g)$.

The condition `orderOf φ = p` is not part of this definition; it is assumed separately. -/
def IsSplitting (φ : MulAut G) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

/-- The subgroup $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ of $G$
generated by the images of $g$ under $\varphi^0, \varphi^1, \ldots, \varphi^{p-1}$. -/
def orbitClosure (φ : MulAut G) (p : ℕ) (g : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin p => (φ ^ (i : ℕ)) g)

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Inversion on an abelian group satisfies the splitting identity for $p = 2$:
$g \cdot g^{-1} = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplitting_inv_two (A : Type*) [CommGroup A] : IsSplitting (MulEquiv.inv A) 2 := by
  intro g
  simp [List.range_succ]

/-- The subgroup $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ contains $g$
when $p \neq 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem self_mem_orbitClosure (φ : MulAut G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ 0) (g : G) :
    g ∈ orbitClosure φ p g :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨⟨0, Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hp⟩, by simp⟩

/--
Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ are nilpotent?

Here $p$ is a prime, a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$ (no periodicity
is assumed), $\varphi$ has order exactly $p$, and each subgroup
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}}\rangle$ is nilpotent, of a class that may
depend on $g$.
-/

    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p) →
      ∀ φ : MulAut G, orderOf φ = p → IsSplitting φ p →
        (∀ g : G, Group.IsNilpotent (orbitClosure φ p g)) → IsLocallyNilpotent G := by

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ are nilpotent?

An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is called *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^2} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

Here $g^{\varphi}$ denotes the image $\varphi(g)$ of $g$ under $\varphi$. The group $G$ may be
infinite, and a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$. A group is locally nilpotent
if all of its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.59»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun H _ => H.isNilpotent

/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi$ has order exactly $p$ and $g \varphi(g) \varphi^2(g) \cdots \varphi^{p-1}(g) = 1$
for all $g \in G$. -/
def IsSplittingAutomorphism (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  orderOf φ = p ∧ ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

/-- Inversion is a splitting automorphism of order $2$ of the cyclic group of order $3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingAutomorphism_inv_zmod_three :
    IsSplittingAutomorphism 2 (MulEquiv.inv (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))) := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun g => by simp [List.range_succ]⟩
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  refine orderOf_eq_prime (by ext g; simp [pow_two]) fun h => ?_
  have := congrArg (fun ψ : MulAut (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)) => ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)) h
  simp at this
  exact absurd (congrArg Multiplicative.toAdd this) (by decide)

/-- The subgroup $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ of $G$ generated by
the images of $g$ under $\varphi^0, \varphi^1, \ldots, \varphi^{p-1}$. -/
def orbitSubgroup (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) (g : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin p => (φ ^ (i : ℕ)) g)

/--
Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a $p'$-group, that is, a group with no element of order $p$.
Suppose that $G$ admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$, i.e. an automorphism of
order exactly $p$ with $g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^2} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all
$g \in G$, such that for every $g \in G$ the subgroup
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ is nilpotent. Is $G$ then locally
nilpotent?

The nilpotency class of $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ may depend
on $g$; no uniform bound is assumed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] (φ : MulAut G),
      p.Prime → (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p) → IsSplittingAutomorphism p φ →
      (∀ g : G, Group.IsNilpotent (orbitSubgroup p φ g)) →
      IsLocallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.59»
